reference_sql:
SELECT o.store_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY o.store_id
alternatives: WITH order_units AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.store_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(u.units) AS units FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_units u ON u.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.store_id
SELECT o.store_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM order_lines ol RIGHT JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id GROUP BY o.store_id

other_way.sql: WITH order_units AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.store_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(u.units) AS units FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_units u ON u.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.store_id
other_way.tradeoff: Adding up the lines per order first keeps one row per order, so COUNT(*) counts orders, at the cost of one more step.

solver.query:
WITH order_units AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT o.store_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, COALESCE(SUM(ou.units), 0) AS units
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_units ou ON ou.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY o.store_id
